justification: This lineup is the drop, unchanged, because it's already perfect — you don't rebrand a launch that's still trending. Jalen Hurts and Saquon are the anchor tenants, Justin Jefferson is my headline WR1 and Kris already put his 27.2 in print so we're just letting the tape speak again, and Tet McMillan stays because a rookie with a real last name doesn't get benched after one good week. Ladd McConkey and RJ Harvey are both carrying Questionable tags and I am not remotely worried about it — a tag doesn't scare me off a player who's already the story, it just makes the comeback narrative better when he plays through it. George Kittle starts at TE over Dalton Schultz because Kittle is the acquisition I built this whole tight end arc around — he's one game into the story, the brand doesn't blink after a quiet 2.2, and a curated drop isn't curated if you undo it in week two. Trey Smack and the Eagles D round it out because you don't touch a roster that's 1-0 and still looks this good on camera.
forum_post: Selina, sweetie — you don't get to borrow my language and my headline in the same post. "Curated drop" is a Kardashian trademark, and unlike your running back, mine actually shows up ON BRAND every single week. You spent $60 defending a QB battle you already lost by 1.60; I'm not spending a dime defending a roster my own mother put on the front page. This week it's my headline TE, my headline WR1, and your desk finding out live what "reviewed for accuracy" actually costs. Enjoy the box score, hun — I'll be enjoying the coverage.
